mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.10 percentage points over the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% triggers a market reaction to deteriorating labor market conditions, causing a sell-off in equities as corporate earnings growth faces headwinds, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader consumer demand contraction; this combination predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy faces a demand shock.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST decline in prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both RSAFS and HOUST decline in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 100, the manufacturing sector contraction signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate profits face downward pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates strong labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 persons, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 5.0% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as real interest rates rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 265, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS indicate a tightening monetary policy cycle driven by inflation concerns, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase in prior month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong consumer demand as measured by residential investment (RSAFS) above 600,000 million dollars, the housing market expansion supports overall economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 600000, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
